lectures.title: Reform movements: Brahmo Samaj, Arya Samaj, Ramakrishna Mission and other bodies

parts.t: Raja Ram Mohan Roy and the Brahmo Samaj
items: **Atmiya Sabha:** Raja Rammohan Roy, 1815; monotheism / religious and social reform.
**Brahmo Samaj:** founded by Raja Rammohan Roy at Calcutta, 1828; one God, anti-idolatry; monotheism; opposition to social evils.
**Brahmo Samaj opposed** idol worship, Sati and child marriage.
**Aim of Brahmo Samaj:** social & religious reform; women's education.
**Motto / key phrase (Brahmo Samaj — Raja Rammohan Roy):** universal worship of one God.
**Raja Rammohan Roy:** associated with Brahmo Samaj and the abolition of Sati.

**Brahmo Samaj (1828)** is the first social reform movement, the first major socio-religious reform movement and the first religious reform movement of modern India; its founder is Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
**Prarthana Samaj:** founded by Atmaram Pandurang at Bombay, 1867; social and religious reform.
**Aims of Prarthana Samaj:** oppose caste system; widow remarriage; women's education; reform marriage customs.
**M.G. Ranade:** Prarthana Samaj; social reform; Indian National Social Conference.
**Indian National Social Conference:** aim to abolish polygamy, child marriage & patriarchy.
**Seva Sadan:** Ramabai Ranade; women's welfare / education.

parts.t: Dayanand Saraswati and the Arya Samaj
items: **Arya Samaj:** founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati at Bombay (Mumbai), 1875; Vedic revival / Vedic reform.
**Aim of Arya Samaj:** revival / reform based on the Vedas; social reform.
**Slogan:** “Back to the Vedas” / “Go Back to the Vedas” (Swami Dayanand Saraswati, Arya Samaj).
**Arya Samaj slogan:** “India is for the Indians”.
**Dayanand Saraswati** is called the **Martin Luther of India**.
**Ramakrishna Paramahamsa:** religious reform; unity of religions; Hari, Ram, Allah, Christ → different names for the same God.
**Vivekananda's philosophy:** Vedanta; pure Vedanta + truth of all religions.
**Ramakrishna Mission (Ramakrishna Movement):** founded by Swami Vivekananda at Calcutta, 1897; service, education, social reform.
**Ramakrishna Mission:** a social / spiritual movement; non-political + non-sectarian + humanitarian.
**Aim of Ramakrishna Mission:** service to humanity / practical Vedanta.
**Motto (Ramakrishna Mission — Swami Vivekananda):** “Atmano Mokshartham Jagad Hitaya Cha” — for one's own liberation and for the welfare of the world.

parts.t: Theosophical Society and other reform bodies
items: **Theosophical Society:** founded at New York, 1875, by H.P. Blavatsky & H.S. Olcott; spiritual / religious reform.
**Motto of the Theosophical Society:** Universal Brotherhood of Humanity.
**Manav Dharma Sabha:** Durgaram Manchharam, 1844, Surat; social / religious reform.
**Radha Swami Satsang (Radhasoami Satsang):** Shivdayal Sahab, 1861; Satnaam + Anami.
**Aim of Radhasoami Satsang:** one God, importance of Guru / Satsang and spiritual life.
**Dev Samaj:** Shiv Narayan Agnihotri, 1887, Lahore; religious / social reform.
**Sarvodaya Samaj:** Vinoba Bhave; Gandhi's principles / refugees.
**Servants of India Society — Gopal Krishna Gokhale:** service of India / constitutional methods.

lectures.title: Reform movements: anti-caste, Muslim reform, education and the press

parts.t: Jyotiba Phule and the Satyashodhak Samaj
items: **Jyotiba Phule:** anti-caste reformer; belonged to the Mali community; lower-caste upliftment.
**Satyashodhak Samaj:** founded by Jyotiba Phule at Pune (Maharashtra), 1873; anti-caste / social equality.
**Aim of Satyashodhak Samaj:** upliftment of backward classes; liberation of Shudras & Ati-Shudras.
**Shudras + Ati-Shudras:** main beneficiaries of the Satyashodhak movement; liberation from exploitation.
**Motto / key phrase (Satyashodhak Samaj — Jyotiba Phule):** truth-seeking / social equality.
**Gulamgiri:** Jyotiba Phule's work; criticism of Brahmanical domination.
**Sarvjanik Satyadharm Pustak:** Jyotiba Phule's work; anti-caste thought.
**Deenbandhu:** spread the Satyashodhak movement to remote parts of Maharashtra.
**Savitribai Phule:** head of the women's section of the Satyashodhak Samaj; worked for lower-caste girls; women's education.
**First Woman Teacher in India:** Savitribai Phule.
**First Girls School in India:** opened at Pune (1848) by Savitribai Phule and Jyotirao Phule.
**Home for Widow:** established by D.K. Karve at Poona, 1896.
Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi, Rashid Ahmad Gangohi & others
Religious education and reform among Muslims

parts.t: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and Aligarh
items: **Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College (MAO):** Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, Aligarh, 1875; promotion of modern Western / scientific education among Indian Muslims.
**MAO College (1875):** original name Madarsatul Uloom Musalmanan-i-Hind.
**1877:** name changed to Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College.
**Aligarh Muslim University (AMU):** Aligarh, 1920; MAO College became AMU.
**Tahzeeb-ul-Akhlaq:** journal of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan; Urdu; 1870.

parts.t: Colleges and universities of the reform era
items: **Hindu College:** Raja Ram Mohan Roy + David Hare; Calcutta; 1817.
**Hindu College** was an early modern educational institution, established before Delhi College, Mayo College and MAO College.
**Deccan Education Society (Deccan Educational Society):** Agarkar (G.G. Agarkar) + Tilak + Chiplunkar + Namjoshi — 1884; Pune; nationalist education; Fergusson College (1885).
**Central Hindu School:** Annie Besant; Banaras; 7 July 1898; later became a centre of development of BHU.
**Banaras Hindu University (BHU):** Madan Mohan Malviya; Varanasi / Banaras; 1916; established through the efforts of Malviya with the cooperation of Annie Besant.
**BHU foundation stone:** laid by Lord Hardinge II on 4 Feb 1916, on Basant Panchami.
**BHU (1916):** first Central University among the given options.

lectures.title: Reform movements: firsts, reform laws and books

items: **First Anti-Sati Campaign:** led by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, the first social reformer against Sati.
**First law against / abolishing Sati:** Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829.
**First Widow Remarriage Movement:** led by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, the first social reformer to champion widow remarriage.
**First Widow Remarriage Act:** Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (Widow Remarriage Act), 1856.
**First legal measure against Child Marriage:** Age of Consent Act, 1891.
**First Special Marriage Law:** Special Marriage Act, 1872.
**First Social Reform Movement:** Brahmo Samaj (1828); founder Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
**First Religious Reform Movement of Modern India:** Brahmo Samaj.
**First Major Socio-Religious Reform Movement:** Brahmo Samaj (1828); founder of the first reform movement: Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
**First Youth Organisation of India:** Young Bengal Movement.
**Founder of First Youth Reform Movement:** Henry Louis Vivian Derozio.
